context.description: A context to match, or * for any context.

ComputedValue.description: A ComputedValue as the trilean package represents it; validated by the runner of the package that owns it.

context.description: A context to match, or * for any context.

Function.description: The built-in functions a `call` case may name.

Json.description: Any JSON value. An object with a $number member is the number it names and has no other member; a $number member holding anything but one of the four names is refused.

context.description: A context to match, or * for any context.

NonEmptyText.description: A text that holds at least one code unit.

ParseError.description: What the refusal is pinned to: its index, fragments of its reason, or both. At least one, since an empty error is satisfied by any refusal for any reason.

index.description: Offset in UTF-16 code units into pattern. Given only where the case pins it.

message.description: Fragments the reason text of the refusal contains, each after the end of the one before.

PostfixKind.description: The postfix operators of a regex node, which take one operand.

RegexNode.description: A trilean-regex abstract syntax node, with the field names of the package's ast module. An unbounded repeat omits max.

ranges.description: The positive set; never empty, since a class holds at least one item. Each range's from is not above its to, which the schema cannot express and every loader checks.

oneOf.description: max is omitted for an unbounded repeat. min is not above max, which the schema cannot express and every loader checks.

astSubset.description: A partial regexNode for astSubset: an object that matches when every key it gives matches (an array matches element by element at the same length, any other value when equal). It names at least one key, since an empty subset matches every tree.

RelayedText.description: The text exactly, character for character; or, where it holds a message another package wrote (the parse error of a pattern, which the corpus of that package pins), what comes before that message, its parts, the separator the implementation writes between them, and what comes after. The text is the concatenation, compared exactly.

SchemaName.description: The export names of the schemas of the package that a `validate` case may name.

SerialiseSchema.description: The tree and value schemas a `serialise` case may name.

SimpleKind.description: The regex nodes that hold nothing.

Skip.description: Names the implementation that skips the case, for a case one implementation cannot run: ts for a case the TypeScript implementation skips, rust for a case every build of the Rust implementation skips, wherever it runs (native, or wasm under Node, a browser or Workers). Always with a reason.

SpecialName.description: The name of a number the canonical JSON form cannot hold.

SpecialNumber.description: A number the canonical JSON form cannot hold, written as an object: a negative zero (a canonical form writes it as 0), an infinity or NaN.

SqlCollectionBinding.description: The correlated table a collection key maps onto, the caller's SQL relating it to the outer row, and the columns a reference key inside its `item` and `filter` maps onto.

SqlColumnBinding.description: What a reference key maps onto: a column, dot-qualified, and optionally its declared kind.

SqlConnection.description: How the SQLite connection is prepared. `regexpFunction: false` leaves the `regexp` function unregistered.

SqlError.description: The failure an operation ends in. `name` is the package's error class; `CallerError` is the exception the options' callback threw, which must reach the caller unchanged.

SqlExecuteExpect.description: What an execute case expects: the ids a tree selects, the rows a statement returns, or the failure of the query, as fragments of the engine's own message.

SqlExecuteOptions.description: The options of a compilation an engine runs: the dialect is the case's own, so the options never name one.

SqlOptions.description: The options of a compilation as data: the maps stand in for the `columnFor` and `collectionFor` callbacks, and a key a map lacks makes the callback throw.

SqlParam.description: A positional parameter with the kind the dialect binds it as.

SqlParamType.description: The declared value kind of a mapped column, which a comparison against the column is checked against.

SqlPatternError.description: What a pattern a dialect cannot express is refused with: the exact text of the refusal.

SqlRun.description: What to run: a tree compiled for the case's dialect and run, a tree only the evaluator reads, or a statement.

Subject.description: What the tree is evaluated as.

Text.description: A string as a sequence of UTF-16 code units, which is what the TypeScript implementation and the patterns' index counts are in. A JSON string, which must be well-formed Unicode so every loader can read it, or an object holding the code units themselves for content a JSON string cannot carry, an unpaired surrogate.

Tolerance.description: How far a number may be from the one a case gives. Numbers compare exactly unless a case gives a tolerance: `ulps`, the number of representable doubles between the two numbers, or `absolute`, a distance the two numbers must be strictly closer than. A tolerance holds for every number in the value that is compared, treats both zeros as one value, and never applies to an expectation that is not finite.

description: One corpus file: an object holding a non-empty list of cases. Every case names the behaviour it pins with a unique id and a from, and takes a kind-specific shape. See README.md for the rules a schema cannot express.
